current_activity: Tractable: attacks towards the Laison on the left of the Canadian columns to protect their flank
notes: Event date: 14 August 1944, noon (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 425, 430). Event definition: At noon on 14 August the division of I Corps, on the left of the 3rd and 4th Canadian Divisions, attacks towards the Laison to protect the Canadian flank; it had come back under I Corps with the 33rd Armoured Brigade when the inter-corps boundary was swung south during the four days of the earlier Canadian attack, 7-10 August (p. 425; Stacey dates it 9 August, CR0852). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 430: "At the same time the 51st Division of I Corps, on their left, also attacked towards the Laison to protect the Canadian flank"; p. 425: "I Corps had taken the 51st Division and 33rd Armoured Brigade under command again". Location: Soignolles, Calvados (new place), the Canadian start line with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Soignolles on the Caen-Falaise road; the division attacked on the left, some miles to the east. Location support: Ellis places the Canadian start line on either side of Soignolles and the 51st Division on its left (p. 430); no closer place is given for the division.
